title: Germany Ausbildung: Complete Guide for International Applicants
excerpt: How paid vocational training in Germany works, who qualifies, language requirements, and how to prepare a strong application file.
author: SK Immigration Services
content:
Ausbildung is Germany's dual vocational training system — you learn at a company and a vocational school at the same time, while earning a monthly training salary.

Who can apply?

International applicants from any country can apply if they meet employer and visa requirements. Typical expectations include secondary education, basic German (A2–B1), and a clean background check.

What you earn during training

Training salaries commonly range from €900 to €1,350 per month depending on the field and region. After qualification, wages rise significantly.

Popular fields

  • Nursing and healthcare
  • Hospitality and hotel management
  • Mechatronics and industrial trades
  • IT and retail operations

How we help

SK Immigration Services supports profile screening, CV preparation, employer matching, document attestation, and visa file guidance.

title: Study Abroad Without IELTS: Realistic Pathways in 2026
excerpt: Many universities accept alternative English proof. Here is how to find IELTS-free routes without falling for fake promises.
author: SK Immigration
content:
Not every strong student has IELTS ready. The good news: several destinations offer English-taught programs with alternative language assessments.

Common alternatives

  • Medium-of-instruction letters
  • University internal English tests
  • Interviews with admissions teams
  • Pathway / foundation programs

Important caution

"No IELTS" does not mean "no English ability." Consulates and universities still expect you to study successfully in English (or the local language).

title: Document Attestation Checklist: Musadaqa, Apostille, MOFA & QVP
excerpt: A practical checklist for educational and personal document legalization for Gulf, Europe, and global use.
author: SK Immigration Services
content:
Wrong attestation order is one of the most common reasons files get delayed. Use this sequence as a starting point — your destination country may require a specific path.

Typical flow

  1. Notary / local attestation
  2. Higher education or relevant ministry attestation
  3. MOFA / MFA
  4. Embassy attestation or Apostille (as applicable)
  5. Translation (sworn) if required
